concepts.name: TGIF Weekly Range Retracement Model
rules: On Friday, after the market has completed its weekly expansion toward HTF liquidity targets, expect a TGIF retracement back into the weekly range.
Target a retracement depth of 20% to 30% (ideally ~25%) of the total weekly range established up to Friday morning.
Confluence for the 20%-30% retracement target often aligns with key reference levels such as the previous week's high or previous month's high.
The Friday high typically forms during the morning session between 9:30 AM and 10:10 AM Eastern Time.
entryCriteria: Confirm that weekly expansion targets (e.g., previous week/month high) were reached earlier in the week.
Observe the 9:30 AM RTH open and monitor the 9:50 AM – 10:10 AM macro window for peak formation.
Identify order flow failure, such as price respecting a rejection block or failing to close above a premium wick's consequent encroachment.
Wait for a displacement below a BSSI/FVG, creating an Inversion Fair Value Gap.
Enter short on a return into the Inversion FVG, Bearish Suspension Block, or Silver Bullet setup window.
concepts.invalidation: Candle bodies closing above the Friday morning high or above the consequent encroachment of the bearish inversion array.
quotes: It's likely to go into TGIF, which is retrace back down into the weekly range, 20 to 30%.
You have to know your extraction point. You have to know how the smart money is going to leave the marketplace.

concepts.name: Guarded Liquidity Identification
rules: Relative equal highs or buy-side liquidity pools are not always swept; smart money may guard them during distribution phases.
If price approaches relative equal highs during key macro windows (e.g., 9:50 AM – 10:10 AM) and respects a rejection block rather than breaking out, the buyside is guarded.
Order flow confirmation occurs when candle bodies refuse to close above key rejection levels or upper halves of premium wicks.
entryCriteria: Monitor price approaching relative equal highs near a key timing window (9:50-10:10 AM macro).
Observe candle bodies failing to close above the rejection block or previous wick's consequent encroachment.
Confirm breakdown through an existing FVG to signal an inversion and active guarded distribution.
concepts.invalidation: Candle bodies closing above the relative equal highs or rejection block level.
quotes: How do you know when they're not going to take out relative equal highs? ... We have a macro time... If they guard it during the macro... it gives up the ghost.

concepts.name: Continuous Contract HTF Bias & Draw on Liquidity
rules: Always begin weekly and monthly bias analysis on a Continuous Futures Contract to avoid rollover gaps and distorted key levels.
Map previous month's high/low and previous week's high/low across continuous data and blend with front-month contract data.
Determine the Draw on Liquidity by evaluating path of least resistance from the weekly open relative to nearest HTF liquidity pools in the direction of dominant order flow.
entryCriteria: Mark continuous contract previous month and week extremes on the weekly chart.
Note the position of the current week's opening price relative to those levels.
In a bullish order flow regime, if price opens closer to previous week/month high, establish that as the primary draw on liquidity.
concepts.invalidation: Market structure shift breaking opposing key HTF swing points against dominant order flow.
quotes: My analysis always begins with a continuous contract... Continuous contract gives me a field of reference for key highs, key lows, inefficiencies...

So, if we're opening here, is it more likely that we're going to go to the previous week's high or previous month's high... Clearly, it's easier to get to it here. So, this is the path of least resistance.

summary.summary: This lecture details ICT's weekly price cycle framework for determining market bias, identifying the draw on liquidity, and executing Friday TGIF retracement setups. By starting analysis on continuous futures contracts to establish key weekly and monthly levels, traders can determine order flow direction and utilize macro time windows (9:50–10:10 AM) alongside Inversion FVGs and Rejection Blocks to trade expected 20–30% weekly range retracements.
